_comment: Publication contract for everxyz OCCT build artifacts.
The bucket, region, endpoints, object key layout and transport encoding are
NOT ours to choose: they are the tracked Engineering Asset Supply contract
declared in the Utopia repository (third_party/engineering-assets.json,
schema utopia-engineering-assets.v1). This file restates the subset an OCCT
build job needs so the workflow does not have to read another repository.
Artifacts land in the already-declared SDK supply bucket. No new bucket is
created -- reusing the tracked one is required by Utopia's
maintain-engineering-assets contract, which says to reuse the tracked
provider, bucket and rights context rather than propose new ones.
Sharing that bucket is safe despite it holding Utopia's production assets,
because keys are content-addressed: an object key is a pure function of the
bytes, so an OCCT artifact cannot land on a key another asset would use, and
--forbid-overwrite makes a digest collision fail loudly instead of
clobbering. What is NOT shared is the RAM role: Utopia's
UtopiaSdkSupplyPublish is not reused, because handing an OCCT build job
Utopia's publish identity would widen its blast radius well past this
repository. OCCT gets its own role with the same narrow policy shape.
Consuming these artifacts is out of scope here. Utopia currently rebuilds
OCCT 8.0.0.p1 from the locked upstream source and reads nothing from OSS for
it; whether that changes is a decision for the Utopia side.
Every value is overridable at runtime by the matching OCCT_OSS_* repository
variable, so the target can be repointed without a code change.
Declared and owned by Utopia as 'buckets.sdk'. Pre-existing: the setup
script verifies it and refuses to create it.
bucket.name: everxyz-utopia-sdk-supply-cn-shenzhen

_comment: Expected properties of the tracked bucket, for verification only. Nothing
here is applied: changing settings on a bucket this repository does not own
would be a cloud mutation outside its remit.

publication_contract.digest_covers: the plaintext artifact, before transport encoding

_comment: GitHub OIDC federated into RAM via sts:AssumeRoleWithOIDC. This is the
closest available analogue to Utopia's ACK RRSA path: the workload proves
its identity with a short-lived OIDC token and receives short-lived STS
credentials. No static AccessKey is stored in this repository, which is
also Utopia's rule -- never ask for a long-lived AccessKey.
Utopia's other mechanism, aliyun-cli OAuth, is for humans at a terminal and
cannot work unattended on a runner. It is what provisions this, once.
The role is OCCT's own, deliberately NOT Utopia's UtopiaSdkSupplyPublish:
Utopia's contract requires read, publish and cleanup roles stay separate,
and the same reasoning keeps this repository's publisher separate again.
